stem: Which flow type is used when a user needs to be guided through a series of questions on screen?
explanation: Only screen flows display screens for user input.

stem: When an opportunity is set to Closed Won, an Installation record must be created automatically. Which flow type fits?
explanation: A record-triggered flow starts when a record is created, updated or deleted.

stem: An admin needs a flow to run every Monday at 06:00 to create reminder tasks. Which type fits?
explanation: A schedule-triggered flow starts at a set time and frequency.

stem: Which flow type is a reusable piece of logic that other flows or Apex can call?
explanation: Autolaunched flows have no trigger or screens and are called by other automation. A subflow is an autolaunched flow.

stem: A record-triggered flow only needs to set a field on the same record that started the flow. Which option is the most efficient?
explanation: Before-save flows update the triggering record without an extra database operation and are the fastest option for that job.

stem: Which of these requires an after-save record-triggered flow rather than before-save?

options.text: Setting a field on the triggering record

explanation: Before-save flows cannot create or update other records. After-save flows can create related records, send emails and call actions.

stem: Which statement about the order of execution is true?

options.text: Before-save flows run before validation rules
Validation rules run before any flows
After-save flows run before validation rules
Flows never run when a record is saved

explanation: In the simplified order: before-save flows, before triggers, validation and duplicate rules, then after triggers and after-save flows.

objective: Build a flow from core elements
stem: What is the purpose of entry conditions on a record-triggered flow?

options.text: To run the flow only when certain field values are met
To limit which users are allowed to edit the flow
To rename the flow when it is saved
To give the flow a new version each time it runs

explanation: Entry conditions stop a flow running for every change and help to prevent unwanted automation and loops.

objective: Build a flow from core elements
stem: Which element lets a flow take different paths depending on a condition?
explanation: A Decision evaluates conditions and sends the flow down matching outcomes.

objective: Build a flow from core elements
stem: Which element sets or changes the value of a variable?
explanation: An Assignment element sets values in variables, such as adding a record to a collection.

objective: Build a flow from core elements
stem: Which element reads records from the database into a flow?
explanation: Get Records finds records based on conditions and stores them in variables.

objective: Build a flow from core elements
stem: A flow must update 50 related records. What is the best-practice design?

options.text: Loop through the collection, add changes to a collection, and update once outside the loop
Put an Update Records element inside the loop so that each record is saved as it is handled
Create a separate flow for each of the 50 records and call each one by name
Use a screen flow that a user must run 50 times, once for each record

explanation: Putting data elements in a loop risks governor limits. Collect changes and save once after the loop.

stem: What does a fault path do?

options.text: Handles an error when a flow element fails
Skips validation rules so that the flow can finish
Speeds up a flow by running elements at the same time
Controls which users are allowed to run the flow

explanation: A fault path routes the flow down an error route so you can log the problem, notify someone or show a friendly message.

stem: How can an admin test a flow without saving any changes to the data?

options.text: Use Debug with the roll-back option
Run it as a screen flow only

explanation: Debug lets you run a flow with test inputs, and you can choose to roll back so no data is saved.

objective: Build a flow from core elements
stem: How many versions of a flow can be active at the same time?
explanation: Each save creates a new version, but only one version can be active.

stem: When a flow fails, who receives the default error email?

options.text: The person who last modified the flow
The CEO of the company, as the top role in the hierarchy
Every system administrator in the org, at the same time
No one, because flow failures are silent unless logged

explanation: Salesforce sends flow error emails to the user who last modified the flow, so plan fault paths too.

objective: Explain the retirement of legacy tools
stem: Which statement about Workflow Rules and Process Builder is correct?

options.text: Salesforce ended support for them on 31 December 2025 and recommends Flow
They are the recommended tools for building new automation
They were never supported by Salesforce for production use
They are only available in Developer Edition orgs

explanation: Salesforce retired support for both tools at the end of 2025. New automation should be built in Flow, and the Migrate to Flow tool helps convert old ones.

objective: Explain who the flow runs as
stem: Which statement about record-triggered flows and security is true by default?

options.text: They run in system context, so they can touch data the user cannot
They always respect the user's field-level security

explanation: Record-triggered flows run in system context by default, so design them carefully.

stem: A manager needs a multi-department, multi-step process spanning weeks. Which tool is designed for this?
explanation: Flow Orchestrator organises automation into stages and steps across people and time.

stem: Which problem is a sign of poor automation design?

options.text: A flow updates a field that triggers another flow that updates it back
A flow updates a field that triggers another flow which updates it back again
A flow has a clear name that describes the purpose of the flow
A flow has a description that explains what it does and who owns it

explanation: Automations that trigger one another can loop. Entry conditions and a register of automation help prevent it.

objective: Build a flow from core elements
stem: Which element lets a flow reuse another flow?
explanation: The Subflow element runs another autolaunched flow, which keeps logic reusable.

objective: Build a flow from core elements
stem: What does a collection variable hold?

options.text: Exactly one record from the object
A user's password, held as text
A page layout assigned to the user

explanation: A collection variable stores many values or records. A record variable stores one.

stem: Before building a flow, what is the best first step?

options.text: Write the rule in one sentence and check what already runs on that object
Create the flow and activate it straight away, then check what else runs on the object
Delete the other automation on the object so the flow is the only one
Ask users to test the new flow in production before it is documented

explanation: A clear rule and knowledge of existing automation prevent conflicts, which are the most common cause of flow bugs.

objective: Explain who the flow runs as
stem: Which permission or access does a user need to run a screen flow?

options.text: Access to run the flow, such as the Run Flows permission or flow access via profile or permission set
Modify All Data in the system permissions of their profile, which is always required
Author Apex, so that the Apex actions in the flow can be called from it
View Setup and Configuration, so that they can open Flow Builder and run it

explanation: Users need permission to run flows. A screen flow can then run in user or system context depending on its settings.

stem: A field on the same record must be set when the record is saved, using the fewest resources. Which flow type fits?

options.text: A record-triggered flow run before the save
A record-triggered flow run after the save

explanation: Before-save flows update the triggering record without extra DML, so they are fastest.

stem: When an Opportunity closes won, a related Installation record must be created. Which flow fits best?

options.text: A record-triggered flow run after the save
A before-save flow, because it runs before the record is saved
A screen flow that a user starts from the opportunity page
A scheduled flow that runs every night for closed opportunities

explanation: Creating related records needs the record Id, so it is done after the save.

stem: Every night, all open cases older than 5 days should get a task for a manager. Which tool fits?
explanation: Scheduled flows run on a schedule against a set of records.

stem: A record-triggered flow sometimes fails when a required field is blank, and the user sees a generic error. What should the admin add?

options.text: A fault path that logs the error and shows a clear message
A new page layout with the required field moved higher up
A new profile with Modify All Data so the flow always runs
A larger heap size so the flow can process blank values

explanation: Fault paths let a flow handle errors gracefully and tell someone what went wrong.
